Regenerate deliberately; every value here is a reviewed wire contract consumed BY BOTH codecs from this one path: the TypeScript test src/__tests__/vex-agent/mcp/pipe-front-frames.test.ts and the Go test bridge/internal/front/frames/frames_test.go. No copy of this file exists anywhere.

frames.name: hello

payload.timeoutRefusalBytes: {"v":1,"ok":false,"code":"malformed","message":"Vex Studio: the handshake line did not arrive within 5000 ms."}

frames.note: The bootstrap frame: generation 0, sequence 1 on plane 3. The six numbers are frozen equality checks the front refuses to adapt to.

frames.name: refuse

payload.bytes: {"v":1,"ok":false,"code":"locked","message":"Vex is locked, still starting, or shutting down."}

frames.note: Main authors every byte an external peer sees; the front relays them without composing a word.

frames.name: lock
frames.note: Priority: the front processes LOCK before any queued frame, and every ADMIT still queued names the old epoch and is purged.

frames.name: quit
frames.note: deadlineMs is what REMAINS of main's one absolute 5000 ms budget, never a fresh 5000.

frames.name: ping
frames.note: A u64 above 2^53: proves the decoder reads sequence and nonce as BigInt / uint64 rather than a float.

frames.name: refuse at the control payload bound
frames.note: Payload is exactly 4096 bytes (2 length + 4094 UTF-8), the control bound. One byte more is length_over_bound.

frames.name: hello_ack
frames.note: Header generation is still the bootstrap 0; the payload carries the fresh non-zero generation every later frame must use.

frames.name: bound with every flag verified
frames.note: 0x07 = rejectRemote | firstInstance | messageMode, all three READ BACK from the created handle.

frames.name: bound with an unverified flag reported as zero
frames.note: A flag the front requested but could not confirm is reported 0, never echoed. Main decides what to do about it.

frames.name: open
frames.note: No client pid and no sqos: advisory diagnostics are out of scope for v1.

frames.name: write_done
frames.note: The greatest plane 5 sequence this connection's writes are acknowledged THROUGH. Cumulative: it releases every window byte up to and including it, and the seam's write callback settles only when it covers a logical write's final sequence.

frames.name: peer_closed peer_eof
frames.note: Main delays the close edge until its plane 6 decoder has delivered through sequence 4.

frames.name: peer_closed commanded_close
frames.note: Structural only. Main maps it to its latched lock/vex_quit cause, or to disconnect; the front never authors a domain cause.

frames.name: error
frames.note: A code from the frozen closed set (section 6.5) and a count. No string: peer bytes and paths never travel in a structural counter.

frames.name: data at the data payload bound
frames.note: chunkBytes exactly. One byte more is length_over_bound.

frames.name: data one byte
frames.note: The smallest legal DATA. Zero bytes is empty_data.

frames.name: end main to front
frames.note: The relay's end(): close the writable side of the pipe handle, leave the readable side open.

frames.name: end front to main
frames.note: The peer's FIN. Main raises the seam's `end` with the writable side PRESERVED (duplex-transport.ts).

frames.name: bad magic
frames.note: One bit off VEXF. There is no resynchronisation: the position in the stream is unknown.

frames.name: bad generation
frames.note: A frame from the front main just killed, still sitting in the OS pipe buffer, is malformed by construction.

frames.name: flags bit set
frames.note: All eight bits are reserved in v1. A v1 reader that ignored one would let a v2 sender believe it was understood.

frames.name: control length over bound
frames.note: The hex is the 28-byte HEADER ALONE. The bound is enforced at header parse, before one payload byte is retained.

frames.name: data length over bound
frames.note: Header alone, same reason: a decoder that buffered first would let one length field pin 4 GiB.

frames.name: sequence gap
frames.note: The decoder expects 1 and is handed 5. A pipe does not reorder or drop, so a gap is an unrecoverable framing fault.

frames.name: sequence exhausted
frames.note: 2^64-1 is refused even when it is the expected next value, so a wrap can never reissue sequence 1 as a valid replay.

frames.name: data type on a control plane
frames.note: DATA is a defined type and is not carried by plane 3.

frames.name: control type on a data plane
connection zero on a data plane
frames.note: The data planes never carry a frame with no connection; a zero there is a framing fault, not an addressing convention.

frames.name: connection set on LOCK
frames.note: LOCK names no connection. A non-zero id would suggest a per-connection lock, which does not exist.

frames.name: pause with a trailing byte
frames.note: There is no room in v1 for an unknown trailing field, the same fail-closed decision as flags.

frames.name: refusal bytes are not valid UTF-8
empty data frame
frames.note: A zero-byte write conveys nothing and would give a broken sender an infinite supply of legal frames.

frames.name: hello_ack with generation zero
frames.note: The whole point of the field is to leave the bootstrap generation behind.

frames.name: hello with an unknown sddl kind
frames.note: 1 is the only policy v1 defines. The SDDL itself is compiled into the front, never handed to it as a string.

frames.name: bound with a reserved flag bit
precedence: bad magic outranks a set flag bit
frames.note: Both rules are violated. The magic is checked first, so the magic is what an operator's log names.

frames.name: precedence: a set flag bit outranks a set reserved word
frames.note: flags and reserved are both non-zero; flags is the earlier check.

frames.name: precedence: a set reserved word outranks an unknown type
frames.note: Type 0x00 is defined nowhere, but the reserved word is read first.

frames.name: precedence: an unknown type outranks a bad generation
frames.note: unknown_type and type_not_on_plane cannot both hold - a byte that is no type at all is on no plane - so the pair proven here is the unknown type against the next satisfiable rule.

frames.name: precedence: a type off its plane outranks a bad generation
frames.note: DATA never travels on a control plane, and the generation is stale too. The plane check is the earlier one.

frames.name: precedence: a bad generation outranks an exhausted sequence
frames.note: A frame from the front main just killed, carrying the unreachable sequence as well.

frames.name: precedence: an exhausted sequence outranks a sequence gap
frames.note: 2^64-1 is also not the expected 1. Exhaustion is named first because it says the stream can never continue, where a gap only says this frame is wrong.

frames.name: precedence: a sequence gap outranks an over-bound length
frames.note: Sequence 2 while 1 is expected, and a length far past the control bound. Neither byte of the payload is read either way.

frames.name: precedence: an over-bound length outranks a zero connection
frames.note: The bound is enforced from the header alone, ahead of the connection rule, which is what keeps the retention bound real.

frames.name: precedence: a zero connection outranks an empty DATA payload
frames.note: The header phase completes before the payload phase begins, so a DATA frame that is both unaddressed and empty is connection_zero.

frames.name: precedence: a payload too short outranks a string past the payload
frames.note: REFUSE needs 2 fixed bytes for its u16 length prefix and carries 1. The fixed part is measured before the tail is walked.

frames.name: precedence: a string past the payload outranks invalid UTF-8
frames.note: The declared 16 bytes run past the frame, and the 3 bytes that are present are not UTF-8 either. The length is checked before the bytes are decoded, so no decoder ever reads past the frame.

frames.name: precedence: invalid UTF-8 outranks trailing payload bytes
frames.note: The string decodes first and fails; the trailing byte after it is never reached.

frames.name: precedence: trailing payload bytes outrank the type's enums
frames.note: BOUND sets a reserved flag bit AND leaves a byte over. The frame's own length is authoritative, so the layout fault is reported.

frames.name: error with a code outside the frozen set
frames.note: The front's structural codes are a CLOSED set, so main treats an unknown one as malformed rather than logging a number nobody can read. 0 is defined nowhere.

streams.name: one logical write in three chunks, then a half-close
streams.note: The matching WRITE_DONE on plane 4 names throughSequence 3, the LAST chunk of the logical write, not the END. The chunks here are deliberately BELOW chunkBytes so the fixture stays reviewable; the 32768-byte boundary is pinned once, by the 'data at the data payload bound' frame vector.

streams.name: the front's control answers for one connection's whole life
streams.note: The generation switches from the bootstrap 0 to the negotiated value at the frame AFTER HELLO_ACK, and never goes back.

streams.name: two connections interleaved on the shared upstream data plane
streams.note: The plane's sequence is the PLANE's, not the connection's: 1,2,3,4 across two connections. Fairness is one 32 KiB chunk per connection per turn.

streams.name: cumulative acks for one multi-chunk write
streams.note: One logical write of five plane 5 chunks, acknowledged in three cumulative steps: through 2, through 4 (the front coalesced two completed chunks into one ack) and through 5. Main releases window bytes at each step, so its outstanding bytes never reach 65536 even inside this one write; the seam's write callback settles only at the third, which is the write's FINAL sequence. A regression to one ack per logical write cannot produce this stream.

streams.name: five chunks of one logical write, then a half-close
streams.note: The plane 5 side of the cumulative-ack stream above. The chunk payloads are four bytes each so the fixture stays readable; the 32768-byte chunk bound has its own row. END costs no window and carries no payload.

validationOrderUnsatisfiablePairs.why: A byte that is no type at all is on no plane, so no frame violates both. The unknown type is proven against the next satisfiable step instead.

empty_data is reachable only for DATA, which has no fixed part to be short of, no strings and no enums - so it leads no pair at all. It is discharged as the LATER half of connection_rule > empty_data, which is the boundary between the header phase and the payload phase.
